notes: Mobile Cycle 3 (M2) at 3.25.0: on-device supervision. An agent run on the phone now writes its S1 task record as it goes: created when the run starts, updated at every step boundary and approval wait, so the record is live truth instead of an end-of-run summary. Alongside it the run saves its resumable context (goal, plan, staged changes, step trail) on the D2 checkpoint rails, size-capped like the house precedents. If the app is closed or Android stops it mid-run, the Tasks panel shows the record as Interrupted with when it was last updated and offers Resume: a new run segment briefed from the record's summary, never a replay, counting against the same per-task step budget, with the full history kept in the record. When a run waits for an approval while the app is in the background, a notification names the task and the waiting approval, never a command or file contents; tapping it opens the app at the pending approval, decided by the same in-app buttons as always. A foreground service runs while an agent run is active, but nothing promises a run survives the app being killed: the copy says so, and resume is the answer. Desktop runs are unchanged. Mobile Cycle 3 (S1) at 3.24.0: portable task records. One format (ghostide.task, defined in docs/TASK_FORMAT.md) now describes a unit of agent work on both platforms: every agent or plan run leaves a task record beside its D2 run record (same writer, same run), stored under .ghostide/tasks/ in the workspace and validated strictly and identically by the desktop and phone servers. A record carries the goal, the status, the step budget in force, the approvals summary, the step summary and the checkpoint link; a newer format version is refused by name, never mangled. Records export as a single JSON file and import on the other platform unchanged except a fresh local id, with the mapping kept in the record's provenance. The Tasks panel (Tools) lists, views, exports and imports them, and says plainly that a record is data: resuming a run from a record arrives with supervision (M2). The phone server also gains the record routes the D2 run history always needed on-device. Mobile Cycle 2 (M7) at 3.23.0: voice-to-prompt in the chat composer. The composer mic now runs the phone's in-process speech recogniser: partial results stream into the prompt box while you speak and the final transcript replaces them, as ordinary editable text. Voice never sends a message, never runs the agent, and never acts as a command in the composer; the G13 spoken commands stay where they always lived, on the editor's dictation button. A status line under the composer states in plain words which recognition is in use (the on-device recogniser on Android 12 and up where the phone offers one, whose audio stays on the phone; otherwise the system speech service, which may use the network) and names every way a session can end: no recogniser available, microphone permission off (with the Settings path to grant it), the service needing a network it cannot get, nothing heard, or the recogniser busy. Cleanup is light and visible: whitespace is tidied and a missing space after sentence-ending punctuation is restored; words are never rewritten and spoken punctuation is never converted. The editor dictation path is unchanged. Mobile Cycle 2 (M6) at 3.22.0: phone model guards. The phone's model store (the native Models screen) now reads the device it is on: total RAM from the activity manager and free storage, printed on the store and download screens, with a fit mark per model from the desktop store's own bands. The first-run default model is the largest model that fits this phone's RAM (the 1.5B on a 4 GB phone, the 3B on 6 GB and up), never the 7B; an install that already has a model keeps it. The 7B stays in the store with a plain caution (Large for a phone: expect heat and fast battery drain) instead of a fit mark. Before a model download starts, and before the 7B loads, a hot phone or a battery at 20 percent or less and not charging draws a warning with a go-ahead choice; nothing is ever blocked, and a signal the phone cannot report claims nothing. Agent runs on the phone default to 25 steps instead of 50 (each step is a full on-device generation); any budget picked in Chat options wins on both platforms, and the web model store panel on the phone now points at the native store instead of showing a server error. Mobile Cycle 2 (M4) at 3.21.0: the git phone pack. Git account tokens on Android now live in a Keystore-encrypted store (Settings, Git accounts): the page can save a token and ask whether one exists, but can never read it back, and the on-device server resolves it by remote host at git time - nothing is written into a repo, a remote URL, or page storage, and a token saved by the old panel flow is moved into the store automatically. Clones are shallow by default (depth 1, one branch) with a Full clone opt-in, on both servers. The conflict editor gains a card view at phone widths (one block per card, ours/base/theirs stacked, same choices and save path), and the phone server gains the D9 conflict endpoints and status fields it was missing. Mobile Cycle 1 (M5) at 3.20.0: the Android app checks itself for updates - a separate android-latest.json manifest on the downloads host, compared by versionCode against the installed build (read from the package manager into /api/health). A newer build raises a dismissible banner whose Download button hands the APK to the system browser; the app never downloads or installs anything itself. Automatic checks run at most once a day, Later snoozes one version, and every failure is silent unless you check by hand. Mobile Cycle 1 (M3) at 3.19.0: a slim symbol row docks under the editor at phone widths while it has focus - Tab, brackets, quotes and the everyday code symbols in one sideways-scrolling row, with Undo and cursor keys; bracket and quote keys insert through the editor's own auto-close, so pairs land with the cursor inside. The key set and an on/off toggle live in Settings, Phone. A touch pass lifts tab close buttons, view bar items, panel header buttons and Git row buttons to a 40px minimum target on phones. The M1 viewport gate now also proves the row: it appears on focus, inserts, measures clean, and hides on blur. Mobile Cycle 1 (M1) at 3.18.0 added the viewport-matrix gate and phone layout hardening. Desktop 3.17.0 added git depth (hunk staging, three-pane conflict editor); 3.15.0 the neural embeddings index; 3.14.0 MCP polish; 3.12.0 language servers.
